evidence.note: Server exited before binding port; agent diagnosed the actual cause (missing `requests` package) rather than guessing, and revised the design to make `requests` optional with a urllib fallback for notification delivery — a genuine diagnose-and-fix of the real cause.

Second server exit traced to missing Flask; agent correctly identified the dependency gap and installed requirements to enable local smoke testing. Reactive, correct root-cause handling of an environment divergence.

After generating the app, agent pre-emptively revised several local design choices (presigned UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD default, CopyObject storing wrong bytes, cross-tenant PutObject policy authorization) — but these were self-identified from code review, not driven by falsifying evidence.

Edge tests reportedly passed on first run; agent added list_object_versions/lifecycle/failed-admin-audit patches. No foundational assumption (SigV4, storage/locking) was ever falsified — notably concurrency/load was never tested, so no divergence surfaced there to correct.

reasoning: When checks failed (server exits from missing dependencies), the agent consistently diagnosed the actual underlying cause and fixed it, occasionally revising local design choices (requests→urllib fallback, CopyObject bytes, policy model) — squarely matching anchor 5. However, there is no evidence of anchor-8 behavior: no foundational assumption like SigV4 signing or the storage/concurrency model was ever falsified by testing (boto3 smoke tests passed, load was never exercised), so the agent had no opportunity to demonstrate design-level pivots propagated across subsystems. Behavior lands at 5.
